newsitem.title: FRANCE: Text of French statement on Thomson privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Text of French statement on Thomson privatisation.

text.p: Following is the text of a French Finance Ministry statement on the suspension of the privatisation of Thomson SA (Reuters translation).

"The privatisation commission informed the finance minister on December 2 that it was not in a position to give a favourable opinion on the preference expressed by the government for the privatisation of Thomson SA. In accordance with the law, the government has therefore decided to suspend the privatisation procedure.

The offers gave rise to a thorough inter-ministerial examination and led the government to express on October 16 its preference for the offer of Lagardere Groupe and to inform the privatisation commission, which -- in accordance with the law of August 6, 1986, as amended to take account of privatisations -- had to offer a view on the value of Thomson and issue an opinion on the conditions of the sale and the choice of buyer.

In the conclusions of Bernard Ducamin, the privatisation commission did not criticise the way the procedure had been conducted. Concerning the interests of the state, the Commission's analysis led it to exclude neither of the two offers. However it declared itself unable to give a favourable opinion on the Lagardere Groupe offer, because of the terms of Daewoo Electronics' purchase of Thomson Multimedia. This decision, which was made known to the minister of finance on December 2, will be published in the Official Journal.

As a result, the government has decided to suspend the privatisation procedure. The government will issue a decision quickly the conditions in which the privatisation process will be pursued. It considers this privatisation is indispensable to the company's development and the creation of a world-class electronics industry sought by the president (Jacques Chirac), and to employment and to the preservation of leading-edge technologies within the group.

In this new context, it will be up to the companies concerned to take account of the opinion of the privatisation commission. In the meantime, the government wishes to continue consultations with the European Commission on the conditions for a recapitalisation with remains necessary."
